content_metadata.description: An analysis of a video featuring James Randi discussing fraudulent bomb detectors and the consequences of their use, particularly focusing on James McCormick and the ADE651.

qAndA.answer: Nothing but a lump of hardened epoxy with dead ants embedded in it.
qAndA.question: What was found inside the Quadro Tracker when it was examined by Sandia Labs?
What was the name of the company that created the Quadro Tracker?

qAndA.answer: They learned that a retired FBI agent had purchased a franchise from Quadro.
qAndA.question: What prompted the FBI to finally investigate the Quadro Tracker?

qAndA.answer: He offered them the JREF million-dollar prize if they could prove the device worked.
qAndA.question: What did James Randi offer to the Royal Engineers who were using the rebranded Quadro Tracker (the Mole Detector)?

qAndA.answer: He said he only cared that "it detects bombs," regardless of whether it functioned through magic or science.
qAndA.question: What did the Iraqi general say he cared about regarding the ADE651?

narrativeProgression.description: James Randi introduces the topic of James McCormick and his fraudulent bomb detection device.
Randi mentions McCormick's arrest and charges of fraud.

mood.description: Angry, frustrated. Randi's tone becomes increasingly critical of the authorities who failed to act on evidence of fraud.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Mood shifts due to the absurdity of rebranding a known fake device.

narrativeProgression.description: Randi provides a news quote highlighting the Sandia National Labs and FBI raising alarm about the Quadro Tracker.
Randi emphasizes that McCormick's device is just another fake, similar to the Quadro Tracker.
Randi clarifies his role in alerting authorities about the Quadro Tracker.
Randi details Sandia Labs' findings on the Quadro Tracker, proving it was a useless device.
Randi criticizes the media and government agencies for ignoring the findings.
Randi describes the FBI's belated investigation into the Quadro Tracker, triggered by a retired agent's involvement.
Randi expresses frustration with the FBI's inaction despite evidence of widespread fraud.
Randi reveals the Quadro Tracker was rebranded as the Mole Detector and was still being sold.
Randi highlights the irony of the Mole Detector being adopted by the Royal Engineers.
Randi describes his unsuccessful attempt to challenge the Royal Engineers with the JREF prize.
Randi transitions back to the topic of McCormick and the ADE651.

scenes.title: Exposing the Quadro Tracker

activities.description: James Randi speaks to the camera.

characterInteraction.description: Randi addresses General Al-Jabiri directly, challenging his claims and decisions.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Critiques the defense and continuous use of the ADE651 by Iraqi authority against evidence.

mood.description: Incredulous, sardonic. Randi's tone shifts to sarcasm as he confronts the general's illogical defense of a fraudulent device.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Mood shifts to sarcasm due to the irrational defense of the device.

narrativeProgression.description: Randi returns to the topic of McCormick and the ADE651, mentioning an Iraqi general's defense of the device.
Randi introduces Major General Jihad Al-Jabiri and describes his press conference with McCormick after a bombing.
Randi quotes Al-Jabiri's statement that he doesn't care about Sandia Labs' findings and trusts the ADE651.
Randi directly challenges the general's logic and highlights the absurdity of his position.
Randi points out that Al-Jabiri ignored Randi's challenge to prove the device's efficacy.
Randi expresses relief about McCormick's arrest but urges a firm prosecution.
Randi encourages viewers to demand accountability from McCormick and highlights the consequences of his fraud.
Randi concludes by suggesting that authorities consult with the JREF or similar organizations for expert advice on fraudulent devices.

scenes.thematicElements: Deception, responsibility, the cost of credulity.
scenes.title: Confronting Defense of Fraud

climax.description: The Iraqi general's defense of the ADE651, despite its proven ineffectiveness, highlights the dangerous consequences of trusting in a fraudulent device.

the news that James McCormick, the man behind the Fersicle ADE651 device that is being
used in terrorist-sensitive areas to sweep, cafes, theaters, guarded checkpoints, military
posts, police stations, and other facilities for explosives, has now been arrested and
charged with fraud. He's made literally millions selling these fake sticks, yet he's been
released on bail. Now the very best thing we can hope for is that he'll bolt to escape
prosecution, become an international fugitive, and be found on an island, somewhere, and
specific. I need to set a few facts straight here, however. Yes, I specifically offered McCormick
the J-Refs million dollar prize long ago. He chose to ignore it as we predicted he would,
but the media have reported that, and I quote, in 1995 the Sandia National Labs and the FBI
raised the alarm over a dowsing rod device called the Quadro Tracker, which they described
as a fraud, and the FBI warned all agencies should immediately cease using the device.
That is quite true, but you should know that the McCormick device is quite the same as
all the other fakes, including the Quadro, and the actual procedure by which this FBI action
arose is a bit different. I was the one who alerted the U.S. Department of Energy, the
DOE, to the Quadro rod, which we'd already tested at the J-Ref with an operator certified
by Quadro using it. Need I tell you that it was useless? The DOE then turned to Sandia
Labs in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and commissioned them to do tests on the Quadro. The Sandia
examination of the device revealed that there were no functioning parts inside the thing,
and that it failed very definitive tests that they performed.
Not to my surprise, the media chose to ignore this finding, as did the CIA, the FBI, and
any and all U.S. government agencies and authorities. Then I got a call from the FBI. Though they
ignored the Sandia DOE findings, they'd learned that one of their retired agents had purchased
a franchise from Quadro authorizing him to sell the device in the state of Florida. That
got FBI attention. One of their own was being victimized. The fact that other American citizens
were being swindled didn't get their attention, but a retired agent did. Well, they moved
in on Quadro, and within 48 hours Quadro was closed down. Why could the FBI not have acted
similarly to protect the rest of us? I even got a phone call from an amused FBI agent
while they were searching the Quadro offices, who told me that they'd found nothing inside
the Quadro rods, but a lump of heartened epoxy with very dead ants embedded in it. I think
that man might have directed his attention, not his humor, at the guilty parties who were
never charged. Ah, but the media just today reported, and I quote,
In 2002, a test by Sandia Labs in the US found that a similar dosing rod device called the
MOL detector, MOLE, did not work and performed no better than a random selection process.
Close quotes. They concluded that it did not work and that it looked nearly identical to the Quadro
tracker. Oh, Contrater, Mesa, me, that was the Quadro. You see, after the FBI raid, Quadro
went out of business, then moved to the UK, and went back into business as the MOLE. They
simply scrubbed off the Quadro name and replaced it with the MOLE logo. This was the same
useless device, the same fraud, but with a crowning glory. Her Majesty's Royal Engineers
bought several of the MOLs and employed them to find smuggled IRA arms. Hearing this, I promptly
sent a formal officer to the Royal Engineers, offering any of them the J-Ref prize if they could
detect anything with the MOLE. Strangely, they refused my offer. Hmm, why, I wonder.
But back to Baghdad, a senior Iraqi officer involved in bomb prevention has defended the ADE-651.
Major General Jihad Al Jabiri, who appeared at a press conference with Mr. McCormick himself,
following a disastrous bombing in which the area had been swept by the ADE-651,
said that he didn't care about Sandia and that he knew more about bombs than Americans. He said,
and I quote, whether it's magic or scientific, what I care about is it detects bombs. Oh, really?

He's running, folks. He's running. They all run. Now, while I'm very happy with the fact that James
Mcleormick has finally been snared by law enforcement, I have to make this appeal to everyone to see
that he is firmly prosecuted. He has a fortune from which he can employ the very best lawyers. He can
